fields.Tool description: Collects public username leads and domain/DNS/IP context in a CLI and web interface. Username outcomes distinguish found, not_found and unknown. Submitted by its developer for independent evaluation.
fields.What it does: Public-profile discovery and infrastructure context for self-audits and authorized research.
fields.How to use it: Run the source-pinned review kit or try a guest web lookup; verify matches at the original source.
fields.Cost overview: MIT-licensed CLI/source; hosted web interface has free guest and paid limits.
fields.Account overview: No for the local CLI or basic guest web checks; some hosted features require sign-in or payment.
fields.Cookies overview: Web analytics/advertising cookies and optional Firebase/browser storage; local CLI contacts upstream sources. See published privacy/cookie policies.
fields.Ownership overview: Aryan Walia / BugSnaps. Contributor is the MyRecon developer; submission prepared with AI assistance.
fields.Reporting overview: Initial lead discovery and infrastructure context; verify attribution and preserve original sources. No independent published case study verified for this submission.
fields.What the tool does: MyRecon is an MIT-licensed Python CLI, Flask API and web frontend for public username leads and infrastructure lookups. The hosted site has separate guest, signed-in and paid limits. Android is maintained separately and its source is not in this repository. Shared usernames do not establish identity or registration availability. This is a developer-submitted description, not an independent test or review. We invite your own testing of failures, unknowns, practical value and limitations.
fields.How to use:
1. Start with the source-pinned review kit: https://github.com/4ryanwalia/Myrecon/blob/97f976bd120488c7ddd26ce444b88f7931a31ed1/docs/review-kit/README.md
2. Run python examples/offline_demo.py for four explicitly synthetic examples; these are not live accuracy evidence.
3. In a fresh Python environment, install the pinned minimal dependencies and run the existing three-platform benchmark with a separate output file, following the kit. It contains ten fixed public/synthetic usernames (30 pairs), timestamped raw results and a blank worksheet.
4. Add your own consented present/absent cases and independent source observations. Record unknowns and errors with denominators.
5. For ordinary CLI use, follow the repository quick start and inspect JSON verdicts. For hosted guest checks, use a username you control and verify each source link.
fields.Cost explanation: The repository is MIT-licensed. Hosted web access is freemium; see https://www.myrecon.xyz/pricing for current limits. Android access differs; no special paid reviewer access or compensation is supplied by this invitation.
fields.Cookies and privacy: The web source and policies describe Google Analytics measurement cookies, possible Google advertising cookies, browser storage for preferences/history, and optional Firebase authentication state. Hosted inputs are sent to MyRecon and configured lookup providers. Local CLI requests contact upstream services from the reviewer network and are not anonymous. This is a source/policy description, not a completed privacy audit. See https://www.myrecon.xyz/privacy.html and https://www.myrecon.xyz/cookies.html.
fields.Use in reporting: Useful to evaluate for initial public-profile lead discovery, a consented digital-footprint self-audit, or DNS/domain/IP context. Confirm account evidence at the platform and corroborate identity separately before reporting. No independently published investigation using MyRecon has been verified for this submission; the provided kit and measurements are first-party. You control whether to publish and what to conclude. No payment, positive review, backlink or endorsement is offered or requested.
fields.Capabilities:
- Public username outcomes with verdict/reason information.
- Domain, DNS, RDAP/WHOIS and IP lookups via source CLI/API.
- JSON CLI output for supported lookups.
- Synthetic offline verdict examples and a reproducible small live regression harness.
- Open repository for inspection and reproducibility.
fields.Limitations:
- Shared usernames are leads, not identity proof or handle availability.
- Login walls, blocks, timeouts and source changes can prevent a conclusion.
- Interfaces have different coverage and access limits.
- Supplied live sample: only ten fixed usernames on GitHub, GitLab and Hacker News; reference shares API evidence with the engine. Not an independent or full-catalogue accuracy audit.
- Sherlock/Maigret packages were not installed for the supplied run; their results are unavailable, not comparative scores.
- No Android device test or independent privacy audit is claimed.
fields.Summary: A candidate for public-profile lead generation and initial infrastructure triage, with inspectable source and explicit unknown outcomes. Its practical value depends on platform availability and manual verification. The supplied developer sample does not establish general accuracy. Please test additional platforms/cases and retain failures in any review.
fields.Ownership: MyRecon is developed by Aryan Walia at BugSnaps; the repository names Aryan Walia and aryan@bugsnaps.in as author/contact. I am that developer and disclose this affiliation. This submission and the review kit were prepared with AI assistance. No independent verification of corporate registration or operator location is claimed in this submission.
fields.Ethical considerations:
- Test only accounts you control or are authorized to investigate.
- Do not attribute accounts to a person using a shared handle alone.
- Minimize collected data and redact private identifiers and credentials.
- Respect provider restrictions and retain inconclusive outcomes.
- Disclose developer affiliation, review access and compensation if any. No compensation or special paid access is offered here.
